t: This is the Serpentine, a forty-acre lake in Hyde Park, created in 1730 at the request of Queen Caroline. Strictly speaking the name belongs only to the eastern half. The long, narrow western half is called the Long Water, and Serpentine Bridge marks the boundary between them. It's named for its snakelike curve. Finbarr Donnelly died here in 1989. He was the singer with the Cork post-punk band Five Go Down to the Sea?, known for his striking stage presence and surreal lyrics.
